summary: Stanislaus NF lookout in Tuolumne County: 1963 steel K-brace replacement of a wooden lookout, fire-season service ended 1971, solar panels added 1987; NHLR-registered 2017.

facts.design: 54-foot steel K-brace tower with a 13 by 13 foot live-in cab; Forest Service standard designs (tower L-1600 series, cab CL-30) and a garage built in 1963

events.note: earlier wooden lookout; history page says 1940, federal survey says about 30 feet tall, a 1940 newspaper said a planned 45-foot tower with glass cab
Register and survey: current 54-foot steel K-brace tower and 13 by 13 foot cab, with a garage
current tower and garage replaced the earlier wooden lookout
continuous fire season service until 1971; Juanita Larson the lookout for the last four years
solar panels added to the cab roof in fall 1987 to power part of the Forest radio repeater system

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A January 1940 newspaper planned a 45-foot tower with a glass cab; the federal survey describes the built wooden tower as about 30 feet tall. Both are reported in the story; the built height is the survey's figure.
The survey's OCR text garbles the year of the wooden tower; the history page gives 1940 plainly, and the 1940 newspaper matches. The story uses 1940.

notes_for_editor: No current access rule, visit report or rental listing was in any of the four pages read. The NHLR page has no visit reports for this tower. The HABS PDF is an OCR text and some digits are garbled (for example the wooden tower year and the 54-foot height), so quotes were chosen from clean text on the history page or the Register. The historic-structures page asks readers for a status update, which is why access stays unconfirmed. The staffing as_of 1971 is the last fire-season year, not a current status. Budget: about six page reads; one web search for rentals returned no direct listing.
